meta.title: Overworld Farming Yield Study v1
meta.purpose: Define the evidence and measurement structure needed to determine whether overworld preparation can sustain the Contested Fort economy.

included: Time required for each farming activity
Preparation capacity for Fort Floors 1, 2, and 3

currentKnownInputs.repairRule: Repair is per weapon. A full restore may require up to 3 discrete Repair_Kit_Basic uses when all three weapons require repair.

fortClearTimes.note: These are study assumptions only and are not authoritative values.

studyQuestions: How much food does an average player obtain during 30 minutes of overworld preparation?
How much water does an average player obtain during 30 minutes of overworld preparation?
How much scrap does an average player obtain during 30 minutes of overworld preparation?
Are repair kits obtained in the overworld, and at what reliable rate?
Which maintenance items are obtained in the overworld, and at what rate?
What time and travel cost is required to collect each resource?
What is the expected failure, interruption, or death risk during farming?
How much preparation is required to support one run on each Fort floor?
Does overworld farming make the intended Floor 1, Floor 2, and Floor 3 loop sustainable?

measurementModel.requiredSamples: Use a minimum of 3 comparable samples per activity when evidence becomes available. Record average, low, and high yield.

yieldReporting.confidence: Mark each value as observed, defined by approved design, provisional estimate, or unknown.

comparisonFramework.profitabilityStatus: Do not label a floor profitable, break-even, or net-loss until resource values and conversion assumptions are explicitly defined.

requiredOutputs: Average, conservative, and best-case yield per 30 minutes
Preparation requirement for each Fort floor
List of values still requiring approval
openQuestions: Whether overworld farming is safe, contested, or interruptible
Whether farming has stamina, travel, or time-window limits

checkFor: Incorrect assumptions against the approved scarcity and economy files
Whether this is the correct next study
